WooCommerce zwykle lepiej pasuje do firm: WooCommerce usually suits a company that develops its sales within the WordPress ecosystem and bases client acquisition on content. PrestaShop is worth considering when the center of the project is an extensive store, its catalog and its commercial processes. The choice between WooCommerce and PrestaShop doesn't come down to comparing feature lists. Both solutions can be extended, but they differ in architecture and the way the store is organized. The decision should follow from the role of content, the complexity of the catalog, the integrations required, plans for selling in many markets and the ability to maintain the system.

WooCommerce rozszerza WordPress o funkcj: WooCommerce extends WordPress with sales features, while PrestaShop is a platform built directly around running a store.<1><2>[2]</2></1><3><4>[5]</4></3> This is the fundamental difference, because it affects the relationship between the content layer and e-commerce operations.
Lepszy wybór zależy od wymagań firmy: st: The better choice depends on the company's requirements: the catalog structure, integrations, selling in many markets, the role of content and the way the system is maintained. This is a decision framework, not the result of an independent benchmark covering all possible builds.
Analizę najlepiej rozpocząć od pytania,: The analysis is best started with the question of what the store is to be for the company. If sales are part of an extensive WordPress website, the natural direction may be WooCommerce. If the project is above all a system for handling the catalog and commercial processes, PrestaShop requires more attention. However, none of these conditions alone settles the questions of costs, integrations or performance.

WooCommerce i PrestaShop mogą obsługiwać: WooCommerce and PrestaShop can serve similar sales goals, but they organize the content layer, the catalog, the store back end and day-to-day e-commerce operations differently.
WooCommerce zwykle pasuje do firm, które: WooCommerce usually suits companies that want to develop sales within an existing WordPress website and rely heavily on content. PrestaShop is worth considering when the center of the project is an extensive store and its commercial processes, rather than primarily WordPress content.<1><2>[1]</2></1><3><4>[4]</4></3> These are scenario-based recommendations. They don't prove that WooCommerce always provides better SEO or a lower cost, or that PrestaShop will be the right choice after a certain number of products is exceeded.

However, this shouldn't be treated as an automatic SEO advantage. The final result still depends on the content, the configuration and the quality of the build.

PrestaShop warto analizować wtedy, gdy c: PrestaShop is worth analyzing when the center of the solution is to be the store, and design decisions follow mainly from the catalog structure and commercial processes. However, this isn't a rule based on company size or a simple threshold of products. The fit should be decided by specific operations, integrations and the development plan.
Przy ocenie katalogu ważniejsza od samej: When assessing the catalog, its complexity matters more than the number of products alone: variants, pricing rules, stock levels, sales channels and connections with other systems. The WooCommerce documentation covers support for, among other things, variable and digital products, cross-selling, up-selling and shipping classes.<1><2>[7]</2></1> However, the presence of these features doesn't mean that every configuration will be optimal for a large or unusual catalog.
Dlaczego liczba produktów nie wystarcza: Why the number of products isn't enough to choose
Dwa katalogi o podobnej liczbie pozycji: Two catalogs with a similar number of items can require different ways of handling them. That's why, before deciding, you should write down the variants, pricing dependencies, stock levels, sales channels and operations carried out by the team. Only such a description makes it possible to judge whether the features needed are available in the core, require an add-on or integration work.
WooCommerce jest przedstawiany przez pro: WooCommerce is presented by its developer as a scalable solution, but actual performance depends on the hosting, code, add-ons, queries, catalog and configuration.<1><2>[6]</2></1> There's also no independent test comparing both platforms under identical conditions, so the developer's claim shouldn't replace testing the target build.
W przypadku każdej wymaganej funkcji trz: For each required feature, you need to establish whether it's in the core, requires a plugin or module, and who is responsible for its updates. The availability and quality of add-ons change over time, so the mere existence of an extension doesn't yet confirm that a specific integration is ready.<1><2>[10]</2></1>

PrestaShop ma funkcję multistore, która: PrestaShop has a multistore feature that lets you manage several stores or groups of stores from one back end.<1><2>[8]</2></1><3><4>[9]</4></3> However, what it can do depends on the configuration, the version and the compatibility of the modules used. A company planning many domains, languages or brands should check which settings will be shared and which separate for individual stores.

Obie platformy mogą być używane bez opła: Both platforms can be used without a fee for the core code, but the total cost depends on the hosting, the build, modules, integrations and maintenance.<1><2>[3]</2></1> Without data from a specific project, it's impossible to honestly say which platform will be cheaper.
Porównanie powinno obejmować ten sam zak: The comparison should cover the same functional scope on both sides. You need to take into account the configuration, data migration, the extensions required, connections with the company's systems, testing, updates and further development. <1>The cost of launching a WooCommerce store</1> alone isn't enough for a comparison if the offer for PrestaShop covers a different scope of work.
Praktycznym rozwiązaniem jest przygotowa: A practical solution is to prepare one specification and give it to contractors for both platforms. That way you can compare the same features, integrations and maintenance obligations, instead of setting two incomparable starting prices side by side.
Decyzję trzeba potwierdzić testem krytyc: The decision has to be confirmed by testing the critical features and agreeing the maintenance model. In WooCommerce, you need to manage updates of the core, extensions and theme, test changes and remove unmaintained add-ons.<1><2>[11]</2></1> This doesn't prove that PrestaShop requires less maintenance work.

If the project includes unusual processes, many integrations or multistore, a general comparison of platforms won't replace an analysis of the target architecture.
Kto odpowiada za aktualizacje i bezpiecz: Who is responsible for updates and security
Firma powinna wskazać osobę lub zespół o: The company should appoint a person or team responsible for updates, testing, backups and responding to problems with add-ons. The budget also needs to include <1>the costs of maintaining a company website</1>, if the store runs as part of a larger website and uses a shared technical back end.
Brak właściciela utrzymania oraz nieokre: The lack of a maintenance owner and an undefined way of testing changes mean that the technology decision isn't complete yet. The platform should be assessed together with the team that will develop it and the procedure for controlling changes.

Podstawowy kod może być używany bez opła: The core code can be used without a fee, but a working store generates costs for hosting, the build, add-ons, integrations and maintenance. Without defining the project scope, it's impossible to state its total cost.
PrestaShop ma funkcję multistore umożliw: PrestaShop has a multistore feature that makes it possible to manage several stores or groups of them from one back end. What it can do depends on the configuration, the version and the compatibility of the modules used.
